Overload.descr: Raise an error with message if v is false or nil; otherwise return all arguments. Returns any — All arguments.
Close a suspended or dead coroutine. Returns boolean, any — true, or false and the error.
A new coroutine running f. Returns thread — The coroutine.
Whether the running code can yield. Returns boolean — true if it can yield.
Start or continue co; the arguments are passed to its function or returned by its yield. Returns boolean, any — true and the yielded values, or false and the error.
The running coroutine. Returns thread, boolean — The coroutine and whether it is the main one.
"running", "suspended", "normal" or "dead". Returns string — The status.
A function that resumes a new coroutine running f on each call; errors are raised. Returns function — The resuming function.
Suspend the running coroutine; the arguments are returned by resume. Returns any — The values passed to the next resume.
Raise an error with message. level 1 (default) adds the position of the caller of the current function, 0 none.
The metatable of object (its __metatable field if set). Returns table? — The metatable.
Iterate over t[1], t[2], ... up to the first nil: `for i, v in ipairs(t) do`. Returns fun(): integer, any — Iterator for a generic `for`.
Absolute value. Returns number — |x|.
Arc cosine, in radians. Returns number — The angle.
Arc sine, in radians. Returns number — The angle.
Arc tangent of y/x, in radians, using the signs of both for the quadrant (x defaults to 1). Returns number — The angle.
Smallest integer >= x. Returns integer — Rounded up.
Cosine of an angle in radians. Returns number — cos(x).
Radians to degrees. Returns number — Degrees.
e to the power x. Returns number — e^x.
Largest integer <= x. Returns integer — Rounded down.
Remainder of x / y, rounded towards zero. Returns number — The remainder.
Logarithm of x to base (default e). Returns number — The logarithm.
The largest argument. Returns number — The maximum.
The smallest argument. Returns number — The minimum.
Integral and fractional part of x. Returns number, number — Integral part and fraction.
Degrees to radians. Returns number — Radians.
Without arguments a float in [0, 1); with m an integer in [1, m]; with m and n an integer in [m, n]. Returns number — The random number.
Seed the random generator (without arguments with a random seed).
Seed the random generator (without arguments with a random seed).
Sine of an angle in radians. Returns number — sin(x).
Square root. Returns number — The root.
Tangent of an angle in radians. Returns number — tan(x).
x as an integer if it has an exact integer value. Returns integer? — The integer, or nil.
"integer", "float", or nil if x is no number. Returns string? — The number type.
Whether m < n as unsigned integers. Returns boolean — true if m < n.
The key after key in t and its value; nil at the end. next(t) == nil means t is empty. Returns any, any — Next key and value.
The API version of this OpenSAK build. Each function lists the version it was added in. Returns integer — The API version.
One cache as a table (see Cache fields). It is a snapshot: changing it changes nothing in the database. Returns opensak.Cache? — The cache, or nil if it is not in the database.

Iterate over caches, one table per cache (see Cache fields), in a generic `for`. Without arguments: the caches of the active filter, in grid order. With filter keys (see Filter keys): the caches matching them, sorted by name; the view and the active filter stay unchanged. `database` reads another database, without switching: its caches matching the filter keys, or all of them, sorted by name. `fields` limits the fields loaded (`code` is always included), which makes loops over many caches faster. Caches are loaded in chunks, so large databases do not hit the memory limit. Returns fun(): opensak.Cache? — Iterator for a generic `for`.
Let the user pick one item of a list. Returns string|number? — The item picked, or nil if cancelled.

Let the user pick a file in a file dialog. The picked file may be used for the rest of this run without a folder permission: read with mode "open" (the default), written with mode "save". OpenSAK's own settings and database files cannot be picked. The dialog starts in the macro file's folder. Returns string? — Full path of the picked file, or nil if cancelled.

Let the user pick a folder in a folder dialog. The macro may then read and write files in it for the rest of this run, without a folder permission. OpenSAK's own folders and whole drives cannot be picked. Returns string? — Full path of the folder, or nil if cancelled.
Remove the corrected coordinates of a cache. Returns boolean — false if the cache is not in the database.
Remove the active filter, so all caches are shown again.
The GC codes of the caches of the active filter, in grid order. Cheaper than opensak.caches() when only the codes are needed. Returns string[] — GC codes.
The columns of a table or view of the active database (or the one named by the `database` option). Returns {name: string, type: string}[] — Column names and SQL types, in table order.
Ask the user a Yes/No question. Returns boolean — true on Yes.
Initial bearing from the first point to the second. Returns number — Degrees, 0 = North, clockwise.
Initial bearing from the first point to the second. Returns number — Degrees, 0 = North, clockwise.
Great-circle distance between two points. Returns number — Distance in km.
Great-circle distance between two points. Returns number — Distance in km.

Format coordinates. Formats: `"dmm"` (default), `"dms"`, `"dd"`, `"utm"`, `"mgrs"`, `"ch1903"` (Swiss LV03), `"ch1903+"` (Swiss LV95), `"rd"` (Dutch RD), `"osgb"` (British National Grid), `"sweref99"` (SWEREF 99 TM), `"gk"` (German Gauss-Krüger), `"olc"` (Plus Code), `"geohash"` and `"maidenhead"`. Aliases: `"lv03"`, `"lv95"`, `"bng"`, `"sweref"`, `"gauss-krueger"`, `"pluscode"`, `"qth"`. The national grids are only meaningful in and around their country; `"osgb"` and `"utm"` raise an error where they are not defined. Returns string — E.g. "N47 22.123 E008 32.456" or "32T E 465123 N 5247123".

Format coordinates. Formats: `"dmm"` (default), `"dms"`, `"dd"`, `"utm"`, `"mgrs"`, `"ch1903"` (Swiss LV03), `"ch1903+"` (Swiss LV95), `"rd"` (Dutch RD), `"osgb"` (British National Grid), `"sweref99"` (SWEREF 99 TM), `"gk"` (German Gauss-Krüger), `"olc"` (Plus Code), `"geohash"` and `"maidenhead"`. Aliases: `"lv03"`, `"lv95"`, `"bng"`, `"sweref"`, `"gauss-krueger"`, `"pluscode"`, `"qth"`. The national grids are only meaningful in and around their country; `"osgb"` and `"utm"` raise an error where they are not defined. Returns string — E.g. "N47 22.123 E008 32.456" or "32T E 465123 N 5247123".

Whether a point lies inside a polygon. The polygon is either a file (GPX track/route/waypoints, KML, or a text file with one coordinate per line; read permission needed, relative paths are resolved against the macro file's folder) or a table of points, each a coordinate string, `{lat, lon}` or `{lat = ..., lon = ...}`. Edges are straight lines in latitude/longitude, as in the line/polygon filter. Returns boolean — true if the point is inside.

Whether a point lies inside a polygon. The polygon is either a file (GPX track/route/waypoints, KML, or a text file with one coordinate per line; read permission needed, relative paths are resolved against the macro file's folder) or a table of points, each a coordinate string, `{lat, lon}` or `{lat = ..., lon = ...}`. Edges are straight lines in latitude/longitude, as in the line/polygon filter. Returns boolean — true if the point is inside.

Offline reverse geocoding with the boundary data used by Update location. A field is nil where no region matches. Returns {country: string?, state: string?, county: string?}? — nil if the boundary data is not installed.

Offline reverse geocoding with the boundary data used by Update location. A field is nil where no region matches. Returns {country: string?, state: string?, county: string?}? — nil if the boundary data is not installed.
The point halfway between two points (along the great circle). Returns number, number — Latitude and longitude of the midpoint.
The point halfway between two points (along the great circle). Returns number, number — Latitude and longitude of the midpoint.

Parse a coordinate string. Without `fmt` the format is detected: latitude/longitude (DMM, DMS, decimal degrees), UTM, MGRS, British grid letters ("TQ 30268 79642"), Plus Codes, Maidenhead locators, geohashes (5+ characters mixing letters and digits) and the Swiss, Dutch, Swedish and German grids as number pairs, which are only accepted inside their country. Pass `fmt` to read one format only — needed for numeric British grid positions, short geohashes and to rule out a wrong guess. Formats: `"latlon"`, `"utm"`, `"mgrs"`, `"ch1903"`, `"rd"`, `"osgb"`, `"sweref99"`, `"gk"`, `"olc"`, `"geohash"`, `"maidenhead"` (`"latlon"` covers DD, DMM and DMS; every name `opensak.coords.format` takes works too). Returns number?, number?, string? — Latitude, longitude and the format that was read, or nil if the text cannot be parsed.
Waypoint projection: the point a given distance away in a given direction. Returns number, number — Latitude and longitude of the projected point.
Waypoint projection: the point a given distance away in a given direction. Returns number, number — Latitude and longitude of the projected point.
Like opensak.move_caches(), but the caches stay in the active database. Returns integer — Number of caches copied.
The number of caches matching the active filter. Returns integer — Number of caches shown.

Create a new, empty database in the default database folder and add it to the list. The active database does not change. Fails if the name is taken or its file already exists. Returns string — The name actually used (surrounding spaces removed).
The cache selected in the grid. Returns opensak.Cache? — The cache, or nil if no row is selected.
The name of the active database. Returns string — Database name.
Whether a database with this name is in the database list (exact, case-sensitive match). Returns boolean — true if it exists.

Overload.retVal: {name: string, path: string, active: boolean, size_mb: number}[]
Overload.descr: All databases in OpenSAK's database list, sorted by name. Returns {name: string, path: string, active: boolean, size_mb: number}[] — One table per database.
Format seconds since the epoch (e.g. from `os.time()` or `opensak.date.parse()`) in local time. Returns string — The formatted date.

Parse a date into seconds since the epoch, the same kind of value as `os.time()`. Without a format, ISO 8601 (`"2026-10-06"`, `"2026-10-06T14:30:00Z"`) and `"06.10.2026 [14:30[:00]]"` are understood. Times without a zone are local time. Returns integer? — Seconds since the epoch, or nil if the text does not parse.

The listing description of a cache. Not part of the cache table because it can be large. Returns {short: string?, long: string?, html: boolean}? — Short and long description and whether they are HTML; nil if the cache is not in the database.
End the macro right away. pcall cannot catch it, and it is not an error: the macro window shows the code, and `opensak --run-macro` exits with it.

Export the caches of the active filter with a saved export setting (File → Export → GPX/LOC/GGZ: format, folder, file name, if the file exists, corrected coordinates, max. caches). The file name variables are filled in as in the dialog, {filter} with the name of the active filter and {center} with the active centre point. The file goes into *folder* if given, else into the setting's folder. That folder needs write permission (Settings → Folder permissions); for an unapproved one the user is asked first. Nothing is written when no cache with coordinates is shown, or when the file exists and the setting says skip (or ask, and the user answers No). Returns string?, integer? — The file written and the number of caches in it; nil if nothing was written.

Export the caches of the active filter without a saved export setting. `path` is the file to write; its name may use the variables of the export dialog ({database}, {filter}, {center}, {date}, {count}, ...), and a relative path is resolved against the macro file's folder. Its folder needs write permission, like opensak.export_file(). `rename(c)` and `description(c)` are called with each cache table (see Cache fields) and return the name and the waypoint description to write (nil keeps the default). With `target = "device"`, the file goes into the GPX or GGZ folder of the connected Garmin device instead (`path` is then only the file name; MTP devices are not supported yet). Nothing is written when no cache with coordinates is shown, or when the file exists and `if_exists` says skip (or ask, and the user answers No). Returns string?, integer? — The file written and the number of caches in it; nil if nothing was written.

Export the caches of the active filter and/or their child waypoints as Garmin POI files (.gpi) with a saved POI export setting (File → Export Garmin POI: folder, file name, if the file exists, which points, name/description/extra templates, category, proximity alert, icon, max. points). The file name variables are filled in as in the dialog. With "one file per waypoint type" a file is written for the caches and one for every waypoint type. The files go into *folder* if given, else into the setting's folder, which needs write permission (Settings → Folder permissions); for an unapproved one the user is asked first. An existing file is skipped when the setting says skip (or ask, and the user answers No). Returns string[]?, integer? — The files written and the number of POIs in them; nil if nothing was written.

Build a filter from the given keys (see Filter keys; combined with AND unless `mode = "OR"`) and apply it. Usually called with table syntax: `opensak.filter{ ... }`. When nothing matches, the view is left unchanged. Returns integer — Number of matching caches (0 = view unchanged).

The name of the active filter: the `label` of opensak.filter{}, a profile name, or "" when no filter is active. The same as the {filter} variable of an export file name. Returns string — The filter name; "" for none.
Apply a saved filter profile. Returns integer — Number of matching caches.

Show a dialog built from a table (see Forms) and wait until it is closed. Fields with a value come back in a table keyed by their `id`. Callbacks such as `on_change` run while the form stays open and can change it through the handle they get. Without `buttons` the form has OK and Cancel. Returns table<string, any>?, string? — The values by field id and the id of the button (or `exit_on_change` field, or "timeout") that closed the form; nil if it was cancelled.
Ask for one line of text. Returns string? — The text entered, or nil if cancelled.
Write a message to OpenSAK's log file and the macro output. Run with `opensak --run-macro`, it goes to stderr while print() goes to stdout.
OpenSAK's macros folder (read permission by default), without a trailing separator. Returns string — Folder path.
Show a message with an OK button and wait until the user closes it.

Move caches from the active database to another one, with all logs, waypoints, attributes, trackables and notes (like Database → Move caches). By default the caches of the active filter. When a cache already exists in the target, `if_exists` decides: `"newer"` (default) replaces it only if the active database's copy was imported later, `"replace"` always, `"skip"` never. A cache not written to the target stays in the active database. Returns integer — Number of caches moved.
The names of all saved filter profiles. Returns string[] — Profile names.

Open a progress window with a Cancel button, for long loops. `p:update(i [, text])` moves the bar to *i* of *total* and returns false once the user has pressed Cancel; `p:close()` closes the window (also done when the macro ends). Without *total* the bar just shows that work is going on. Returns opensak.Progress — The window.

Search for the first match of a regular expression (Python syntax). Each call may run at most 2 s. Returns string?, string?... — The whole match followed by the captures (nil for a group that did not take part), or nil if there is no match.

All non-overlapping matches. Without capture groups each item is the whole match, with one group it is the capture, with several it is an array of the captures. Returns string[]|string[][] — The matches.
Whether the text contains a match. Use `^` and `$` to match the whole text. Returns boolean — true if the pattern matches.

Replace matches. In a replacement string, `\1` or `\g<name>` insert a capture. A replacement function gets the whole match and the captures and returns the new text (nil or false keeps the match). Returns string, integer — The new text and the number of replacements.
Split the text at every non-empty match. Returns string[] — The pieces between the matches.

Read a CSV file (UTF-8) into an array of rows keyed by the header line. A relative path is resolved against the macro file's folder. If the file's folder has no read permission (Settings → Folder permissions), OpenSAK asks the user to allow it for this run or always. The file may be at most 10 MB. Returns table<string, string>[] — One table per data row, keyed by header.
Redraw the cache list, detail panel and map now. Changes a macro makes are otherwise shown when it ends.

Run another macro and wait until it has finished, e.g. to chain several macros from one control macro. A relative path is looked up in the folder of the calling macro, and `.lua` is added when the name has no extension. The called macro gets its own global variables; values are passed as extra arguments (read them with `...`) and come back as its return values. An error in it stops the calling macro too, unless caught with `pcall`. Macros run this way share the run's limits, sleep time and folder approvals; they may call each other at most 10 levels deep. Returns any... — What the macro returns.
Select a cache in the cache list and show it in the detail panel and on the map, like a click on its row. Returns boolean — false if the cache is not among the caches of the active filter.
The GC codes of the rows selected in the grid. Returns string[] — GC codes; empty if nothing is selected.

Set corrected coordinates, either as decimal degrees or as one coordinate string in any format OpenSAK understands (DMM, DMS, decimal degrees). Returns boolean — false if the cache is not in the database.

Set corrected coordinates, either as decimal degrees or as one coordinate string in any format OpenSAK understands (DMM, DMS, decimal degrees). Returns boolean — false if the cache is not in the database.
Remove this macro's saved settings, so the next opensak.settings.load() returns an empty table.

The settings this macro saved with opensak.settings.save(), or an empty table on the first run. Each macro has its own settings, kept per macro file in the `settings` folder of the macros folder; no other macro can read them. A renamed macro starts with empty settings, and an unsaved macro has none. Returns table — The saved settings; empty if there are none.

Save settings for the next run of this macro, replacing the saved ones. Strings, numbers, booleans and nested tables can be saved; a table needs string keys, or 1, 2, 3, … for a list. Functions and cyclic tables are refused, and the settings may take up at most 1 MB.
Pause the macro. One pause lasts at most 10 s and all pauses of a run together at most 60 s; a cancelled macro stops at its next pause.

Sort the cache list, like a click on a column header. opensak.caches() and opensak.codes() then return the caches in this order. Fields: `name`, `code`, `type`, `container`, `difficulty`, `terrain`, `hidden`, `placed_by`, `country`, `state`, `county`, `found`, `found_date`, `dnf`, `dnf_date`, `ftf`, `archived`, `premium`, `distance`, `bearing`, `favorite_points`, `trackable_count`, `user_flag`, `locked`, `user_sort`, `user_data1`, `user_data2`, `user_data3`, `user_data4`.

Run a read-only SQL query (SQLite) against the active database (or the one named by the `database` option) and return all rows. Only reading statements are allowed; the connection itself is read-only. Column names follow the database schema, which may change between versions (see opensak.tables() and opensak.columns()). Use `AS` to name computed columns. NULL values are nil. At most 100,000 rows; use opensak.sql_each() for more. A query is aborted after 60 s. Returns table<string, any>[] — One table per row, keyed by column name.
Like opensak.sql(), but returns an iterator for a generic `for` that fetches the rows in chunks — for results of any size. Returns fun(): table<string, any>? — Iterator for a generic `for`.
Make another database the active one, as the toolbar dropdown does. The active filter is cleared.
The tables and views of the active database (or the one named by the `database` option), for use with opensak.sql(). Returns string[] — Table and view names, sorted.
OpenSAK's folder inside the system temp folder (read and write permission by default), without a trailing separator. "/" works as separator on every platform. Returns string — Folder path.
Cross sum: the sum of all digits; other characters are ignored. Returns integer — Sum of the digits.

Turn HTML (e.g. a cache description) into plain text: tags removed, entities decoded, block elements and `
` become line breaks. Returns string — The text.

Make a string safe as a database or file name on every platform: characters such as `\ / : * ? " < > |` become `_`, white space is collapsed, leading/trailing dots and spaces are removed and the length is limited to 100. Never empty. Returns string — The safe name.
ROT13 as used for hints. Text in [square brackets] stays unchanged, like on geocaching.com. Returns string — The decoded (or encoded) text.
Letter value sum (A=1 … Z=26). Accents are dropped (Ä counts as A); other characters are ignored. Returns integer — Sum of the letter values.
The OpenSAK version this macro runs in. Returns string — Version, e.g. "1.21.0-beta.3".
CPU time used by OpenSAK, in seconds. Returns number — Seconds.
Format a time (default now) with a strftime format; "*t" returns a table, a leading "!" uses UTC. Returns string|table — The formatted date.
Seconds since the epoch, now or for a table {year, month, day, hour, min, sec}. Returns integer — Seconds since the epoch.
Iterate over all keys of t, in no particular order: `for k, v in pairs(t) do`. Returns fun(): any, any — Iterator for a generic `for`.
Call f in protected mode: errors are caught. Returns boolean, any — true and the results, or false and the error.
Write the arguments, separated by tabs, to the macro output pane.
Whether a and b are equal, without calling __eq. Returns boolean — true if equal.
t[k] without calling __index. Returns any — The value.
Length of a table or string without calling __len. Returns integer — The length.
Set t[k] = v without calling __newindex. Returns table — t.
With a number n: the arguments from the n-th on (negative counts from the end). With "#": the number of arguments. Returns any — Arguments or their count.
Set the metatable of t (nil removes it). __gc is not allowed in macros. Returns table — t.
Byte values of s[i] to s[j] (default i = 1, j = i). Returns integer... — The byte values.
A string from byte values. Returns string — The string.
The binary chunk of a Lua function. Returns string — The bytecode.
First match of pattern in s from init; plain turns off pattern matching. Returns integer?, integer?, string?... — Start, end and the captures, or nil.
Format the arguments like C printf: %d %i %u %c %x %X %o %e %f %g %q %s %a %%, with flags, width and precision. Returns string — The formatted text.
Iterate over the matches of pattern in s: `for word in s:gmatch("%a+") do`. Returns fun(): string?... — Iterator returning the captures.
Replace matches of pattern; repl is a string (%1 = capture), a table or a function. Returns string, integer — The new text and the number of replacements.
Length in bytes (same as #s). Returns integer — The length.
s in lower case. Returns string — The text.
The captures of the first match of pattern (the whole match without captures). Returns string?... — The captures, or nil.
Pack values into a binary string by fmt. Returns string — The binary string.
Size of a string.pack result for fmt. Returns integer — Size in bytes.
s repeated n times, separated by sep. Returns string — The text.
s reversed (byte by byte). Returns string — The text.
The part of s from i to j (default end); negative positions count from the end. Returns string — The substring.
Unpack values from a binary string by fmt. Returns any... — The values and the next position.
s in upper case. Returns string — The text.
Join t[i] to t[j] (strings or numbers) with sep. Returns string — The joined text.
Append value to t, or insert it at pos and move the following elements up.
Append value to t, or insert it at pos and move the following elements up.
Copy a1[f..e] to a2[t..] (default a2 = a1). Returns table — a2.
A table with the arguments and n = their count. Returns table — {..., n = count}.
Remove and return t[pos] (default the last element), moving the following elements down. Returns any — The removed value.
Sort t in place; comp(a, b) returns true when a comes first (default <).
t[i], ..., t[j] as separate values (default 1 to #t). Returns any... — The values.
Convert v to a number; with base (2-36) parse an integer numeral in that base. Returns number? — The number, or nil if v cannot be converted.
Convert v to a string (uses __tostring if set). Returns string — The text.
The type of v: "nil", "number", "string", "boolean", "table", "function", "thread" or "userdata". Returns string — The type name.
A UTF-8 string from code points. Returns string — The string.
Code points of the characters from byte i to j. Returns integer... — The code points.
Iterate over the characters: `for pos, code in utf8.codes(s) do`. Returns fun(): integer, integer — Iterator: byte position and code point.
Number of UTF-8 characters from byte i to j. Returns integer? — The count, or nil and the position of an invalid byte.
Byte position of the n-th character (counted from i). Returns integer? — The byte position.
Emit a warning built from the arguments (all strings).
Like pcall, but on error handler is called with the error and its result is returned. Returns boolean, any — true and the results, or false and the handler's result.
